facts.text: Nearly 1.87 million travellers visit Kamloops in 2024, generating a record $316 million in direct visitor spending in the city.
Tourism supports 2,645 jobs in Kamloops in 2024 and brings in $8.5 million in local government taxes, with visitor volume down only 4.5% from the record year.

Interior Health Authority and Thompson Rivers University are the two largest employers in Kamloops, with School District 73, Highland Valley Copper, New Gold, Domtar and the City also major employers.
Kamloops-based tourism produces $382 million in total economic impact across the Thompson-Nicola region in 2024 and $528 million for British Columbia.

overview: Kamloops reached 97,902 residents in the 2021 Census, up 8.4 per cent from 90,280 in 2016, with a median age of 41.6 and a median household income of $88,000 in 2020. Those figures describe a mid-sized, working-age market with steady public-sector paycheques from Interior Health and Thompson Rivers University.

The city stretches across 297.93 square kilometres, so its 39,914 occupied dwellings are spread among separate neighbourhoods on both sides of the rivers. Nearly 1.87 million visitors in 2024 add a second customer base, which means a local business competes for residents and travellers at the same time.
